## The plan/execute split

A conventional warp pipeline reads source data and reprojects it in one step.
**rwarp** separates these into two explicit phases:

1. `warp_plan()` — pure geometry; no I/O. Returns the source windows and
   destination sub-windows needed. Inspect, cache, or parallelise this.
2. `warp_exec()` (or `warp_resample()`) — the actual pixel work, driven by
   a user-supplied `read_fn`.

This means you can:

- **Inspect fill ratios** before deciding whether to fetch data at all.
- **Cache plans** when the same destination grid is reused across many dates.
- **Swap the reader** between GDAL, HTTP byte-refs, Zarr, or in-memory buffers
  without touching the warp logic.
- **Parallelise** by distributing chunks across workers.

## Anatomy of a plan

```{r plan_structure}
library(rwarp)
library(vaster)

## A 10-degree-per-pixel global source
src_gt  <- c(-180, 10, 0, 90, 0, -10)   # 36 x 18 grid
src_dim <- c(36L, 18L)

## A Web Mercator destination at ~156 km/pixel (zoom 1)
dst_gt  <- c(-20037508, 156543, 0, 20037508, 0, -156543)
dst_dim <- c(256L, 256L)

plan <- warp_plan(
  src_crs  = "EPSG:4326", src_gt = src_gt, src_dim = src_dim,
  dst_crs  = "EPSG:3857", dst_gt = dst_gt,
  dst_off  = c(0L, 0L), dst_size = dst_dim
)

cat("Length of plan:", length(plan), "\n")
cat("Chunks in first group:", length(plan[[1]]), "\n")

ch <- plan[[1]][[1]]
cat("\nChunk fields:\n")
str(ch)
```

## Fill ratio

The fill ratio tells you what fraction of the destination window has a valid
source pixel.  Values below 1 indicate that the source does not fully cover
the destination.

```{r fill}
## A high-latitude destination that only partially overlaps the source
## (global geographic source, destination tile near the North Pole in LAEA)
src_gt2  <- c(-180, 1, 0, 90, 0, -1)
src_dim2 <- c(360L, 180L)

dst_gt2  <- c(-500000, 5000, 0, 500000, 0, -5000)   # 1000 km at North Pole
dst_dim2 <- c(200L, 200L)

plan2 <- warp_plan(
  src_crs  = "EPSG:4326",
  src_gt   = src_gt2,
  src_dim  = src_dim2,
  dst_crs  = "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +datum=WGS84 +type=crs",
  dst_gt   = dst_gt2,
  dst_off  = c(0L, 0L), dst_size = dst_dim2
)

if (!is.null(plan2)) {
  cat("Fill ratio:", plan2[[1]][[1]]$fill_ratio, "\n")
} else {
  cat("No overlap (NULL plan)\n")
}
```

## Antimeridian splitting

For source rasters that cross the antimeridian (e.g. a Pacific-centred
projection), `warp_plan()` may return two chunk-lists: one for each side.

```{r antimeridian}
## Pacific-centred destination (centred on 180 E)
dst_gt3  <- c(160 - 180, 1, 0, 10, 0, -1)   # simple illustration
dst_dim3 <- c(40L, 20L)

plan3 <- warp_plan(
  src_crs  = "EPSG:4326",
  src_gt   = c(-180, 1, 0, 90, 0, -1),
  src_dim  = c(360L, 180L),
  dst_crs  = "EPSG:4326",
  dst_gt   = dst_gt3,
  dst_off  = c(0L, 0L), dst_size = dst_dim3
)
cat("Chunk groups (expect 1 or 2 at antimeridian):", length(plan3), "\n")
```

## Tiled execution loop

For large destinations, tile the output and call `warp_plan()` + `warp_exec()`
per tile.  This caps memory usage and enables parallel execution:

```{r tiled_loop, eval = FALSE}
tile_size <- 512L
ncol_full <- 4000L; nrow_full <- 3000L

results <- vector("list", ceiling(ncol_full / tile_size) * ceiling(nrow_full / tile_size))
k <- 1L

for (tx in seq(0L, ncol_full - 1L, by = tile_size)) {
  for (ty in seq(0L, nrow_full - 1L, by = tile_size)) {
    tw <- min(tile_size, ncol_full - tx)
    th <- min(tile_size, nrow_full - ty)

    plan_tile <- warp_plan(
      src_crs = src_crs, src_gt = src_gt, src_dim = as.integer(src_dim),
      dst_crs = dst_crs, dst_gt = dst_gt,
      dst_off  = c(tx, ty),
      dst_size = c(tw, th)
    )
    if (is.null(plan_tile)) next

    tile_result <- warp_exec(
      plan_tile, read_fn,
      src_crs, src_gt, dst_crs, dst_gt,
      dst_size = c(tw, th),
      nodata = nodata
    )
    results[[k]] <- list(result = tile_result, xoff = tx, yoff = ty, w = tw, h = th)
    k <- k + 1L
  }
}
```
